prompt: Implement TargetPainter.paint: fill a white background, then draw centered filled circles of diameters size, 2*size/3, and size/3 in red, white, red -- a classic target.
explanation: fillOval takes the bounding BOX of the ellipse, not its center, so a centered circle of diameter d starts at ((size - d) / 2, (size - d) / 2). Painting has no transparency by default but later shapes cover earlier ones, so drawing the circles from largest to smallest turns three solid disks into rings. This painter's-algorithm ordering is the standard way to build layered 2D graphics.
hints: Start with g.fillRect(0, 0, size, size) in white for the background.
Draw the biggest circle first; each smaller circle covers the middle of the previous one.
For diameter d, call g.fillOval((size - d) / 2, (size - d) / 2, d, d).
